utterances.text: Here in this picture, you cannot see the curve where the bunker was, but the curve would finish around here somewhere, and then down this road - this is the road - that is where these artillery pieces were placed. And I was made to go here in the middle of this area, from where the artillery pieces were firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that spot with a number "1," please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now tell us where the ABiH army was located, where the firing came from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ABiH was on the other bank of Neretva. This is the Neretva River, and the army was on the other side, over here, and in the village of Vrapcici, and the high ground above -- I believe this is the highway. So directly above this highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, could the map be moved down a bit so that we can see again the part which we just saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've talked about artillery. Were there also infantry soldiers of the Convicts Battalion in Rastani? Where were they located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The infantry of that unit, in the course of the night or very early in the morning, came down to the very edge of the village of Rastani where the houses were. And on the map, this would be here, just above these houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark that spot with a "2," please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in that small hamlet of houses, were there also members of the ABiH army present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina controlled that area, and they were in these first houses, and because they were there, the detained men were used so that they would be the first ones to go in and check in these houses whether there were any ABiH soldiers in those houses. Let me just say, I stayed there perhaps an hour or up to two hours in this location which I marked with number "1." There was a soldier there manning a piece of artillery, which was a more recent version of this recoilless gun. They left me there, and they told him that I should be helping him to assemble these projectiles, which consisted of three parts. While I was there, I think that he fired about 15 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this -- after you were there, were you then again taken back to the bunker? What happened at the bunker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were on this spot and that you assisted this soldier with his gun. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was: After you assisted this soldier, were you at one moment taken back to the bunker again, and what happened at the bunker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A soldier came and called us, me and another fellow prisoner who was with me, but who, at that time, was helping another soldier. He was in another location. So they said that we should come to the bunker, and then they told us that the two of us had to go down into the village where the fighting was in progress. At that time, I saw a soldier who had fled the fighting down below. He was asking -- he was begging one - I believe he was one of the commanders - to notify Tuta, as he said, and to tell him that he was sick and that that is why he had come back. And he told him if he learns that you came back from down there, he is going to kill you right away. I saw this soldier. He was close to tears, who also said that he just had a son the day before, that he got a son, and that he could not fight. And commander did not accept that. And then we were ordered that we should take two bags filled with food and that we should go and deliver this food and juices and cigarettes to the soldiers who were in combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you well, so you were given this food and cigarette, and you were asked to move down with your friend to spot number 2, which you've located on the map -- indicated on the map as number 2. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what happened on the way to this location, number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told, "No one will go with you. Go straight down to those houses, and we will follow and observe where you are going," because it could all be seen from up there. This terrain is not forested; this was all burnt and destroyed. So we set off. When we came up 200 metres -- when we were about 200 metres away from the houses, and I was leading, I saw a dead soldier's body. I went ahead for another 100 metres about, and I found another body. One could conclude that these soldiers had been wounded and that they started pulling out in a direction of either the road or the bunker, because one could see how they were taking off pieces of their clothes, jackets, and also rucksack. They still had their weapons next to them. We passed them and arrived at the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what happened when you arrived at the houses? Who did you encounter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of our colleagues came out to meet us. They probably had information that we were coming down with food. We met him --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. You said, "One of our colleagues." Do you mean one of the other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of the other prisoners were there at location number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that location, number 2, there were four. And the two of us were coming down. It was a total of six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did one of your colleagues tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We first asked him, "Are you all alive?" He said that they were. We asked, "Are there any problems? Did the soldiers beat you?" He said that they did not. We said, "So what are you doing?" They said, "We're entering houses. We're searching to see whether there were any ABiH soldiers in the houses, and then these soldiers come in." We reached that first house, first house which was the most exposed. One of the groups of the Convicts Battalion was there. The commander of that group was Kolobara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you also know the first name of this man you have been referring to as Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot recall the name, but it could have been Mario or Marin, but I cannot say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 704, please. I would like the witness in particular to look at page - it's going to be a long number because it doesn't have page numbers - page number 00795361. The English version, page 9. 00795361. Maybe the English version - that's page 9 of the English version - can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the name of the person you have been referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps it was the man listed as number "1," Miroslav Kolobara. On that day, in passing at one point, he told us that in as early as 1992, 1993, while they were with the HVO, when the Bosniaks were with the HVO along with the Croats, he was one of the commanding officers of a unit from Vrapcici from where he was originally. And on that day, he indeed command that unit. Here it says "Miroslav." I said Mario or Marin, and I was not sure about the name, but now I assume that this could be that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's it for Exhibit 704. Thank you. Now, tell me what happened when you arrived at the house where you came across this man Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We delivered this food to them, as well as this juices and cigarettes that we had brought along, and then they had lunch there in this house. And to our four fellow prisoners, they also gave a can of food each. At first, we did not dare say that we had seen two captured soldiers -- sorry, we did not dare say that we had seen two dead soldiers. My apologies. We first told our fellow prisoners this, and they said, "Well, they are already -- there have already been people killed, so they won't make problems to us because of that." When they finished their lunch, Kolobara ordered us to gather up all the dead bodies of the soldiers who were killed there and bring them in front of this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that, when all the bodies were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got those bodies, put them in a cellar, and then they told us to move on. Each one was -- carried also some of the gear - that is, ammunition, grenades, or projectiles for hand-held launchers - and six of us walked several metres ahead of them and were also mingled with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were any of the Muslim soldiers -- were any of those soldiers still in that hamlet where you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We really did not see, but because from above, from the curve, from the road, one has an excellent view of the whole village, left of the Neretva, then it wasn't difficult for them to keep an eye on the soldiers and see when they retreated and where they were retreating. At some point, during the retreat in Rastani, just below the railway track, there is a -- some kind of a passage, a small tunnel, and I think several soldiers - eight, I believe - entered that tunnel while retreating, but since the fire was intensive, they dared not come out into the clearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let me just again take you back to the hamlet where you were. First of all, do you know what the name of that hamlet was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part of the village is called Dumpor's houses, Djumporove Kuce. And let me continue. So together with that group of soldiers and mixed with them, we started down the street. Kolobara told us that we had to turn right. And then on the right-hand side, that is, moving down the Neretva, we went into a house. It wasn't far. It didn't take us long to get there. And we were there for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe if you can be given back the map, 34.2. I don't know if you have it still in front of you. And if you could just mark the route you took. And before you do, could I ask you, when you left the -- this place you've been referring to as Dumpor, what happened -- did anything happen to the houses in Dumpor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As we were going down the street from those Dumpor's houses, towards the Neretva, one of the soldiers, called Splico, had with him a jerrycan with petrol and was setting fire to those houses, one after another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was this soldier named Splico, was that the same Splico you met before in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said he set -- that he set houses on fire. First of all, how many houses did he set on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he put fire to about -- well, between seven and ten houses. These are houses very close to one another. They are in a -- it's a cluster, dense cluster of houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you could put the map on the overhead projector and indicate where those houses were that Splico set on fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These houses are next to number "2." I've already marked it. It's these houses here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle those houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a few more questions on these houses. Do you know whether these houses belonged to Muslims or Croats or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All these were Bosniak houses. In the village of Rastani, as a whole, there was only one Croat household; that is, there were three Croat houses there, but I think they were all in one yard and it was one family there, family Pinjur. The village was mixed. I'd say that 50 per cent were Serbs and 50 per cent Bosniak, or perhaps there were slightly more Serbs there. Serb houses were put on fire, all of them, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were these houses -- when they were set on fire, were they damaged much by the shelling that happened, that occurred on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult, it's really hard for me to say, because I don't remember all the details, but I think that houses burnt in that village that whole day in different places. Some might have been put on fire by shells, but I am saying that I saw that soldier carry around the petrol and set fire to houses one after the other in that part of the village where Dumpor's houses are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, maybe you can now indicate the route you took from the Dumpor houses down into the village. Maybe you can mark with the marker where you went afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to this crossroads and then we turned -- well, I said to our right, because we came from above. We climbed down there. So we were in our -- in these houses. We also entered some houses which had already burned down, either set on fire before or had not burned down completely. But there were -- there was this house which either had never been completed or was very badly damaged - I cannot remember exactly - and that group of ours, which was going headed by Kolobara and another soldier who was slightly older, and could have been in his 50s -- he was in black clothes. He said he was from Matkovici. And all the time while we were in that house, which was about half an hour, he teased us and harassed us and forced us to sing some songs. We were sitting on the stairs inside that house, and then -- and then somebody notified that group, Kolobara or one of them, and said that they had captured two BH army soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then subsequently actually went to the place where these two Bosnian soldiers were kept -- were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark on this map where this was, which route did you take, and where was this location where these two Bosnian soldiers were captured.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I marked the street that we took, the road, and then the street that we took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the circle, that's where you think that these two Muslim soldiers were kept? If that's the case, maybe you can mark that with a number "3," please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me what happened when you arrived on that spot. What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we got there with that group of soldiers and found there another group and two men who were tied, their hands tied behind their backs, and with their faces to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did you find out the names of these two men that were tied up to the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May we go briefly into private session for the names, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, please describe what you saw that -- what happened to these two soldiers. What did you see? Where were you put, and what could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six of us prisoners were very close by. I think that the other group, the other group of soldiers, those who were there, also had a group of prisoners with them and used them as a human shield, just as we had been used that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of these soldiers there joined hands in the harassment and beating of those soldiers. They kept pestering them with questions, asking them, for instance, "How many units does the Bosnian army have?" "Which units are coming from Bosnia?" I remember they asked them how many physicians had arrived from Sarajevo, because it was common fact that on the left bank, there were hardly any physicians left. Then they found some money in their pockets and forced them to eat that money. And then one of those soldiers got hold of that petrol and sprayed one of them on the face and said, "Now, we'll put them on fire." And at that moment, I really thought they'd do that. And then they said -- they communicated that the old man had called, meaning Tuta I guess, and that he had said to bring in the soldiers alive. I think that I was present at this harassment for about one to two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know where these soldiers were taken after all this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw that they took them away live. And after we returned to the Heliodrom, the first time we were visited by the International Red Cross, an official of that organisation, a very polite, very urbane Swiss, we told him that two soldiers had been taken away. We gave him their full names and that they had been taken from Rastani. He invested a lot of effort. He came to see us at the Heliodrom from time to time, and he repeated every time that he absolutely had no information, no idea where those men could be. After about some two months later, that is, sometime in November, a group of prisoners returned. That group had spent a lot of time in Siroki Brijeg, or near Siroki Brijeg, at Tuta's, and they told us that in the cellar of Tuta's headquarters, there were two men incarcerated. We let the International Red Cross know about it right away, that is, the first time that man came to the Heliodrom after we had learned about this. And since it was November, I think they brought some pressure to bear either on that unit or the HVO authorities. But be that as it may, later on, I learned that in late November, those two men were transferred from the cellar at Siroki Brijeg to the prison in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find out why they were transferred from Siroki Brijeg to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know the exact reason, but my guess is since the Red Cross was trying to trace them for a long time, because their names were known because it was known that they had been captured alive and taken away from Rastani, I assume that certain pressure was put so that they could not be hidden any more. And so they were taken to Ljubuski, and I believe that in a very -- that a very short time after that, they were registered by the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, after you had seen this incident in Rastani, is it correct that you then that evening were taken back to the Heliodrom? And I wanted to ask you, were all ten of you taken back that evening to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Six of us returned to the Heliodrom, that is, all six from that group. Three prisoners managed to cross over to the territory controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and one prisoner disappeared during that action that day. And to this day, neither his body has been found nor is there any trace of his being exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That concludes my examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself. I am the counsel for the accused Mladen Naletilic, and I will ask you some questions. Because we both speak the same language, I must ask you to listen to the end of my question and start your answer only then, to help the interpreters to interpret -- to convey to the transcript as best as they can. I'm sure that you are tired too, and I will try to phrase my questions so as to get the shortest possible answers and answers that will be as concrete as possible, and thank you in advance for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, could we go into private session right at the beginning in order to clear up certain matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm so cautious that even when we mention villages and things like that, this is why I forgot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were no incidents either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could say so, there were none. That is, all the way up to April 15. I was clear on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps you did not hear me well. I had asked you all the way to June. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my apology. These incidents started in the middle of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did ABiH take HVO prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such case, if you're referring to my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Bregava Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not aware of any cases of disarming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That the soldiers of the Croatian Defence Council were disarmed by the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm really sorry I have to disappoint you. I'm not aware of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you don't know, you don't know. Witness, please, there's -- it is not a matter of disappointment. We're just searching for truth. Now, how we feel about that really doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You asked me the same question twice. This is why I said it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Witness -- can you tell me, do you know that the military police during April, May, June was looking for deserter, that there was an outstanding order for their arrest? Are you aware of that perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. If you don't know, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about an attack carried out by the ABiH in Rotimlja in early June against the HVO members? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ABiH carried out an attack against the HVO at Rotimlja?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1st or 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true. That was Bajram the 1st and 2nd. I was there at that time. There were no conflicts whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, you never received from your superiors -- you never received from your superior command any task to take up arms and wait for the right moment to join the 4th Corps with your brigades and attack the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My unit was a part of the 4th Corps, but if there were such -- if such orders existed, they could not have been directed to my unit, because it was already part of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Bregava Brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- was part of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, who had armed you? Who had given you weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From what I know, it was the official organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, what are these official organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Let's say between spring of 1992 to spring 1993, which were the official organs who had armed you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, are those questions relevant to the issues in this case? You have still not come to the crucial point of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I always say, if you say that it's not relevant, I immediately pull back. I just thought that it may have been relevant for you because - you said it so well and it always rings in my ear - and there is this saying, Rome was not built in seven days and nothing could have happened by accident. I am just trying to give this Trial Chamber a more objective picture before we present our own case. It would seem as if nothing happened until the 1st of June, 1993. This is what I wanted -- this is the picture I wanted to fill in for you. But if you think this is not relevant -- you see suddenly, somebody remembered to start arresting people. But if you say it's not relevant, I'll just move on, and I will forget all these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me -- very well, we'll skip all these events. And now you've been arrested, and we are moving on to the Heliodrom. Will you please say who it was that arrested you, who took you to the Heliodrom, and who received you at the Heliodrom, and from there on, who had control over you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was arrested by a unit, an HVO unit from Capljina. We were taken to Gabela by the military police. I believe they were also from Capljina. And who took me from Capljina to the Heliodrom, I really am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now who received you at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, we were received by the regular shift of the police and the guards who were there. And throughout my stay at the Heliodrom, the control over us - and I'm referring to the times when we were inside the compound - the control had the military police. I don't know if -- whether the guards, the prison guards, were also part of the military police. Their commander was Ante Smiljanic. And the warden, I believe, was named Bozic. And there were a whole series of guards who played different roles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not -- I hear for the first time somebody, like, talking about the prison police. Did they have white belts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. I did not see them anywhere else except in the prison, so this is why I said that they were prison police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did the military policemen from Capljina look? Did they also have white belts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they have any kind of badges, any kind of insignias on their sleeves? You were with them every day; this is why I ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They probably did, but I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You could leave the Heliodrom even without the knowledge of the military police, or is it -- or did they always -- did they always have to check with you and did they always know where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me give you my experience. It may not be the same as that of the others. I never left the Heliodrom without my names being written down and registered. The times when I left and the times when I re-entered were always registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can agree if somebody were to come here -- and you said that you did go out to go to work and so on. Let's say if somebody would come into the military police and say, "I need such and such number of men," then they would put together a group, register you, and then you would leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same procedure when you came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Except if one or five did not show up, no one would ask why and where they were. Just let me say, in fact, we were there as a count. We weren't even individual numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know this for sure, that no one paid any attention? You see, I'm trying to distinguish between what you know really, what your firsthand experience is, what your assumptions are, what somebody else told you. I see that you're an educated man.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am saying what a common camp inmate could see with his own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're inferring this because you don't know to whom these lists went and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present when the group from Bijelo Polje came back, and five of them had been killed. And the guard read out their names - that is, of those who had left for Bijelo Polje - and then comes to the name of a person who was killed, and the person does not respond, and they say, "Where is he?" And the guard says -- that is, the others say, "He was killed." And they would go to the next one, and he would ask, "Where is he?" "Killed." And so on. And after that -- no one after that asked why he was killed, under what circumstances. And then I don't know what happened with the prison authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you can only say what happened in the hallway, in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that's exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, just for us to understand each other. Because we weren't there, so we are asking you. And is it possible that somebody had also escaped, that it wasn't just people who were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that point, one does not know whether he was killed or escaped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. For these people, they did know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you the same series of pictures that my learned friend Mr. Bos showed you. I'm sorry that I don't have an overall view of the Heliodrom, but we may be able to find one. First of all, do you personally know in which buildings, that is, which buildings were used as the prison at the Heliodrom, or you only know the premises where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know the building where I was from every side. And as for the others, I passed by them. I was coming and going. But you need to know that eight years have gone by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is why I ask you. And the buildings where you said the HV was, you know for sure? This is your personal knowledge? You saw this yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me give you Exhibit 20.2. Can you please take the pointer and show the building where you were. First, where you were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the building in which I was staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me about your assumption where the others were, the other prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, they were here. That is the building -- you cannot see it well. I think that that was the school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's that? In these --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, plus the two gymnasiums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see them in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But perhaps here behind the school building. I am not sure that they can be seen, but they were somewhere around the school, these two gymnasiums.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was in all these other buildings? Because I see there's a whole lot of them. Of course, if you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, these three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we understood that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. There were the two Croatian army units and the one from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the HVO from Konjic had a unit there. And then this white thing I think was the mess hall, the kitchen. And in this area here was another unit -- I believe in this building here, these were the Bruno Busic -- these were sort of the new recruits. But in these hangars over there, if you can just move the picture a little bit -- over here, you see, there are some other hangars there. There were two tanks there, one T-35 and one T-55.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw them personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on what occasion did you go all the way out there to be able to see all this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In all these buildings where the troops were, I entered them at least five times. Some of them I entered 30 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm more referring to these hangars where you saw the tanks. How come you ended up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These tanks passed by hundreds of times, past the prison from the back side. And down there is the entrance. That's where the gate was. And they would go to Jasenica to the Barbar Hill [phoen], and they fired on the positions held by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Bruno Busic unit, as you call them, the new soldiers, they were not Croatian army unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can conclude there was one HVO unit from Konjic, the HV units, and Bruno Busic? That's it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. There were some others, but I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can't recall, you can't recall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there were different units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean HVO units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, what kind of a treatment did you personally receive? What are your experiences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Treatment of me personally?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In principle, it was the same to everyone in this group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it correct? Can we say that it was correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On whose part?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the prison authorities or whoever was in charge of the prison.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really would not like to say anything bad about anyone. I didn't want to accuse them if they didn't do anything. But whatever was going on in the prison, around the prison, when we were taken to the front line --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no, let's not deal with the confrontation line. I'm talking about the treatment. What was the treatment, the food? That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The food as food was horrible. We ate twice a day. In the morning, it was tea with a slice of bread. In the afternoon, it was mostly, I think, one quarter of a loaf, and some kind of a broth, a bowl of some broth. However, there were days, up to two and a half days, when the imprisoned persons were not given anything to eat. I think that that was between the 19th and the 21st of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This only happened once, or several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This happened at the Heliodrom on that one occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you take showers, wash?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were taps in the area -- in this building which we refer to as the central prison. There were several toilets in every area, and there were also basins with hot and cold water, so we could wash and take showers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were going out, did you receive ready-to-go lunches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It depended, but for the most part we did, at the units where we worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were times, not very frequently, but there were occasions when we received some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As I understand, this photo has been marked previously by this witness. Do you have a clean copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is 4.00 now. I am just going to ask to show this to the witness. I'm interested in one building, and then we can continue tomorrow. [In English] Exhibit 20.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's almost 4.00. If you could just show me this, I'm giving you the same photograph that my learned colleague had given you already. Where were, and from when to when, were these units that you said belonged to the Croatian army were stationed? And just show it to us now and we'll mark it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in this building, the building next to it, and in this building. Out of these three, in two was the Croatian army. I believe that it was in this, and in these ones were the Croatian army soldiers. And in this, I believe, was a unit from Konjits. That was an HVO unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. I believe that this is enough for today. I think that it is 4.00. We can continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, not tomorrow. We are going to continue with this witness on Friday morning, 9.30. Witness, I have to give you a piece of advice, as I did with other witnesses. You have to remember that you are still under the oath, so please do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understood your advice, and I thank you for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tomorrow afternoon, we will have another videolinked conference which will start at 3.00 in the afternoon. We will adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
